Name: Severity Matrix Definition
Symptom: Need to classify incidents by impact and urgency
Root Cause: Lack of standardised severity definitions across teams
Mitigation: Define SEV1-SEV4 with clear criteria: users affected / revenue impact / data loss; publish in runbook
Communication Template: SEV[N] — [Service] — [Impact summary]. Status: Investigating. ETA: [time]. Next update: [time].
Postmortem Checklist: 1. Timeline of events 2. Root cause 3. Impact scope 4. Detection time 5. Resolution time 6. Action items with owners and deadlines

Name: IMOC/Incident Commander Role
Symptom: Chaotic incident response with no clear ownership
Root Cause: No designated incident commander; everyone tries to fix simultaneously
Mitigation: Assign IMOC (Incident Manager On Call) rotation; IMOC coordinates and delegates — does NOT debug
Communication Template: IMOC: @[name]. Comms: @[name]. Technical lead: @[name]. Status page updated: [link]
Postmortem Checklist: 1. Was IMOC paged promptly? 2. Was the right technical lead engaged? 3. Were stakeholders informed within SLA? 4. Was status page updated?

Name: Database Failover Incident
Symptom: Primary database unavailable; all writes failing; read replicas stale
Root Cause: Primary node failure; automatic failover took longer than expected due to large replication lag
Mitigation: Configure tighter replication lag alerts; test failover monthly; use synchronous replication for critical data
Communication Template: SEV1 — Database primary failover in progress. Write operations are degraded. ETA for recovery: [time]. Read traffic is being served from replicas.
Postmortem Checklist: 1. What was the replication lag at failure time? 2. Did automatic failover trigger? 3. How long until writes resumed? 4. Was data lost? 5. Were connection pools reconfigured?

Name: Kafka Consumer Lag Spike
Symptom: Consumer group falling behind; processing delay exceeding SLA
Root Cause: Under-provisioned consumers; sudden traffic spike; slow consumer processing; rebalancing storms
Mitigation: Add consumers; increase partition count; profile consumer bottleneck; set max.poll.interval.ms appropriately
Communication Template: SEV2 — Message processing delay in [consumer-group]. Current lag: [N] messages / [time] behind. Scaling consumers. No data loss expected.
Postmortem Checklist: 1. What caused the lag spike? 2. Were there rebalancing events? 3. Was consumer throughput degraded or was it a producer spike? 4. Were downstream systems affected? 5. What's the max acceptable lag?

Name: Memory Leak in Production
Symptom: Gradual memory increase; eventual OOM kill; service restarts
Root Cause: Memory leak in application code — often unbounded caches or connection pool growth
Mitigation: Heap dump analysis; set memory limits and restart policies; instrument with RSS/heap metrics; use profiler to find allocation source
Communication Template: SEV2 — [Service] experiencing elevated memory usage. Automatic restarts mitigating impact. Investigation in progress.
Postmortem Checklist: 1. Which process/container was affected? 2. What was the growth rate? 3. Was a heap dump captured before OOM? 4. Was the leak in application code or a library? 5. What's the fix?

Name: Certificate Expiration
Symptom: TLS handshake failures; all HTTPS traffic failing to affected endpoints
Root Cause: Certificate expired without renewal; monitoring didn't alert or alert was ignored
Mitigation: Automate cert renewal (cert-manager/ACME); alert at 30/14/7/1 day thresholds; maintain certificate inventory
Communication Template: SEV1 — TLS certificate expired for [domain]. All HTTPS traffic affected. Renewing certificate. ETA: [time].
Postmortem Checklist: 1. Why wasn't the certificate auto-renewed? 2. Was there an alert? Was it acted on? 3. How many services were affected? 4. What's the inventory of all certificates and their expiry dates?

Name: DNS Resolution Failure
Symptom: Services cannot resolve hostnames; widespread connectivity failures
Root Cause: DNS provider outage; misconfigured DNS records; TTL too low causing amplification
Mitigation: Use multiple DNS providers; set appropriate TTLs (not too low); cache DNS locally; have IP-based fallback for critical paths
Communication Template: SEV1 — DNS resolution failures detected for [domains]. Impact: [services affected]. Investigating DNS provider status and switching to backup.
Postmortem Checklist: 1. Was it a provider outage or a config change? 2. Which domains were affected? 3. Were cached DNS records used? 4. What's the TTL configuration? 5. Do we have DNS provider redundancy?

Name: Cascading Failure
Symptom: One service failure causing chain reaction across dependent services
Root Cause: Missing circuit breakers; tight coupling; no fallback paths; shared resource exhaustion
Mitigation: Implement circuit breakers; add timeouts on all RPCs; design fallback responses; use bulkhead isolation
Communication Template: SEV1 — Cascading failure in progress. Origin: [service]. Affected: [list]. Circuit breakers activated. Shedding non-critical traffic.
Postmortem Checklist: 1. What was the origin service? 2. Which circuit breakers fired? 3. Were bulkheads effective? 4. What was the cascading path? 5. Were there fallback responses?

Name: Deployment Rollback
Symptom: New deployment causing errors; error rate spike above threshold
Root Cause: Bad code change; incompatible database migration; configuration error
Mitigation: Automated canary analysis with auto-rollback; health check gates; feature flags for quick disable
Communication Template: SEV2 — Rolling back deployment of [service] v[version]. Error rate elevated. Previous version being restored. ETA: [time].
Postmortem Checklist: 1. What changed in the deployment? 2. Was canary analysis running? 3. How quickly was the rollback initiated? 4. Were database migrations reversible? 5. What gate failed to catch this?

Name: Cloud Region Outage
Symptom: Entire region unavailable; multi-AZ not sufficient
Root Cause: Cloud provider region-level failure affecting multiple AZs
Mitigation: Multi-region architecture with automatic failover; DNS-based routing; regional isolation
Communication Template: SEV1 — [Cloud Provider] [Region] experiencing outage. Failing over to [backup-region]. Some data may be stale (RPO: [time]).
Postmortem Checklist: 1. Was multi-region failover automatic? 2. What was the RPO/RTO? 3. Were there data consistency issues? 4. How was traffic rerouted? 5. When was failback safe?

Name: Rate Limiting Incident
Symptom: Legitimate users being rate limited; false positive blocks
Root Cause: Rate limit thresholds too aggressive; shared IP addresses; sudden legitimate traffic spike
Mitigation: Use adaptive rate limiting; whitelist known partners; implement graduated limits; add rate limit headers
Communication Template: SEV3 — Rate limiting affecting some users on [endpoint]. Adjusting thresholds. Affected users can retry with exponential backoff.
Postmortem Checklist: 1. Were the limits correctly configured? 2. Were legitimate users affected? 3. Was this a traffic spike or an attack? 4. Are rate limit headers being sent? 5. Should limits be dynamic?

Name: Data Corruption
Symptom: Incorrect data in database; downstream systems processing bad data
Root Cause: Application bug writing invalid data; migration script error; race condition
Mitigation: Identify scope of corruption; stop the source; plan data repair from backups/audit logs; notify affected users
Communication Template: SEV1 — Data integrity issue detected in [table/service]. Write operations paused. Assessing scope. No further corrupted writes will occur.
Postmortem Checklist: 1. What was the source of corruption? 2. How many records affected? 3. Do we have audit logs to identify exact scope? 4. Can we restore from backup? 5. Were downstream consumers notified?

Name: Third-Party API Outage
Symptom: Dependency on external API failing; features degraded
Root Cause: Third-party service outage or degradation; no fallback implemented
Mitigation: Implement circuit breaker for external calls; cache last-known-good responses; have graceful degradation plan
Communication Template: SEV2 — [Third-party service] experiencing issues. [Feature] is degraded. Serving cached/fallback responses where possible.
Postmortem Checklist: 1. Was the circuit breaker activated? 2. Were cached responses served? 3. Was the degradation graceful? 4. How were users notified? 5. Should we add a second provider?

Name: Blameless Postmortem Process
Symptom: Incidents repeat because root causes aren't addressed
Root Cause: Culture of blame discourages honest root cause analysis; action items not tracked
Mitigation: Adopt blameless postmortem format; focus on systems not people; track action items in issue tracker with deadlines
Postmortem Checklist: 1. Was the postmortem conducted within 48h? 2. Were all stakeholders present? 3. Are action items specific and assigned? 4. Is there a review date? 5. Were previous postmortem actions completed?

Name: Status Page Communication
Symptom: Users don't know about ongoing incidents; support tickets spike
Root Cause: No public status page; or status page not updated during incidents
Mitigation: Maintain public status page (Statuspage/Instatus/Cachet); update within 5 min of SEV1; post RCA within 48h
Postmortem Checklist: 1. Was the status page updated within SLA? 2. Were updates frequent enough? 3. Was the RCA published? 4. Were affected customers notified directly?
